Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] APT37 NarwhalRAT primary C2 — daehoat.com / novel21.co.kr Korean relay domains + IOC IPs · [LLM] APT37 NarwhalRAT secondary C2 — pCloud API with folderid/auth dead-drop parameters · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
APT37 NarwhalRAT spear-phishing — MS account OTP/security alert lure with ZIP attachment AIDelivery Medium
Hunts inbound emails impersonating Microsoft Account security alerts (OTP abuse, abnormal activity) carrying a ZIP attachment that contains the malicious LNK loader. This is the article-specific delivery shape Genians attributes to ScarCruft. Rationale: Subject keywords map directly to Genians' description of the MS account OTP-abuse lure; ZIP attachment narrows to the article's exact delivery shape. Sentinel left blank because EmailEvents has no clean equivalent in the canonical Sentinel tables in this tenant; OfficeActivity does not carry subject/attachment metadata. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/blog/threat_intelligence
ATT&CKT1566.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Microsoft account verification emails that legitimately include reset instructions (rare with .zip attachments)
  • IT-team-sent security awareness training emails referencing 'Microsoft account' and 'OTP'
  • Third-party SaaS vendor security notifications mentioning 'OTP' or 'one-time password'
  • User-to-user mail forwarding screenshots of MS alerts with .zip evidence bundles
Suppression filter
and not (SenderMailFromDomain in ("microsoft.com", "accountprotection.microsoft.com")) and not (AttachmentName has_any ("evidence", "screenshot", "report"))
Response runbook
Triage: Pull NetworkMessageId, render the original message, examine attachment SHA256 against VT/MISP, and check whether the recipient extracted/opened the LNK. Contain: Soft-delete the message tenant-wide via Microsoft 365 Threat Explorer, block sender domain/IP at the connector, and disable the recipient account session if extraction is confirmed. Hunt: Pivot on the AttachmentSHA256 across all mailboxes (EmailAttachmentInfo) and check DeviceProcessEvents on the recipient's host for explorer.exe → cmd.exe / wscript.exe chains spawned within 1 hour of receipt.
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| where DeliveryAction in ("Delivered", "DeliveredAsSpam")
| where Subject has_any ("Microsoft account", "abnormal activity", "OTP", "one-time password", "security alert", "account security", "verify your account", "password change")
| join kind=inner (
    EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where FileName endswith ".zip"
    | project NetworkMessageId, AttachmentName=FileName, AttachmentSHA256=SHA256, AttachmentSize=FileSize
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, AttachmentName, AttachmentSHA256, AttachmentSize
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
EmailEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| where DeliveryAction in ("Delivered", "DeliveredAsSpam")
| where Subject has_any ("Microsoft account", "abnormal activity", "OTP", "one-time password", "security alert", "account security", "verify your account", "password change")
| join kind=inner (
    EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where FileName endswith ".zip"
    | project NetworkMessageId, AttachmentName=FileName, AttachmentSHA256=SHA256, AttachmentSize=FileSize
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| project TimeGenerated, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, AttachmentName, AttachmentSHA256, AttachmentSize
| order by TimeGenerated desc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Email.All_Email where (All_Email.subject="*Microsoft account*" OR All_Email.subject="*abnormal activity*" OR All_Email.subject="*OTP*" OR All_Email.subject="*one-time password*" OR All_Email.subject="*security alert*") All_Email.file_name="*.zip" by All_Email.src_user All_Email.recipient All_Email.subject All_Email.file_name All_Email.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Email.All_Email where (All_Email.subject="*Microsoft account*" OR All_Email.subject="*abnormal activity*" OR All_Email.subject="*OTP*" OR All_Email.subject="*one-time password*" OR All_Email.subject="*security alert*") All_Email.file_name="*.zip" by All_Email.src_user All_Email.recipient All_Email.subject All_Email.file_name All_Email.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
APT37 NarwhalRAT LNK loader — explorer-spawned cmd/batch fetching python.org binary + CAT file AIExploitation High
Hunts the multi-stage chain where a user double-clicks the LNK extracted from the phishing ZIP, which invokes cmd.exe to run an intermediary batch script that downloads the legitimate Python binary from python.org and a Windows security catalog (.cat) file used as the in-memory loader. Rationale: Article-specific chain: ZIP→LNK→cmd→batch→python.org+CAT download. Time-window correlation between LNK-spawned interpreter and outbound fetch to python.org or one of the Korean relay domains gives high fidelity. Hashes b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b / 3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08 from the article can be added as supplementary IOC pivots. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/blog/threat_intelligence • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0067/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer launching python installer (.lnk on desktop pointing to python.org installer) from explorer
  • IT-deployed batch scripts referenced from shortcuts in startup folder
  • Corporate software-update tools that wrap MSI installers with cmd-based wrappers
  • Power users invoking custom .bat shortcuts from Desktop for daily automation
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\Public\\Desktop\\", "python-3", "python.msi") and AccountName in ("sccm$", "intune$"))
Response runbook
Triage: Resolve the LNK target with `Get-Item` against the file path (look for unusual targets like cmd.exe /c with embedded payload URLs), then capture the batch script and CAT file dropped. Contain: Isolate the host via Defender Live Response, kill the python.exe / cmd.exe tree, and revoke session tokens for the AccountName. Hunt: Sweep the org for the AttachmentSHA256 from UC1 and for any host that has %APPDATA%\naverwhale or scheduled tasks matching the UC4 naming convention.
let LookbackDays = 30d;
let LnkSpawn = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
    | where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".lnk", ".bat", ".cmd")
        or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has ".lnk"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessId, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
LnkSpawn
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("python.org", "www.python.org", "daehoat.com", "novel21.co.kr", "fe01.co.kr", "webhostingkorea.com", "crwellfood.com")
    | project NetTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
  ) on DeviceId
| where NetTime between (Timestamp .. Timestamp + 10m)
| project Timestamp, NetTime, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
let LnkSpawn = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName endswith @"\explorer.exe"
    | where NewProcessName endswith_cs @"\cmd.exe" or NewProcessName endswith_cs @"\wscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith_cs @"\cscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith_cs @"\powershell.exe"
    | where CommandLine has_any (".lnk", ".bat", ".cmd")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName;
LnkSpawn
| join kind=inner (
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where RequestURL has_any ("python.org", "daehoat.com", "novel21.co.kr", "fe01.co.kr", "webhostingkorea.com", "crwellfood.com")
    | project NetTime=TimeGenerated, Computer=DeviceName, RequestURL, DestinationIP
  ) on Computer
| where NetTime between (TimeGenerated .. TimeGenerated + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, NetTime, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, RequestURL, DestinationIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\\explorer.exe OR *\\EXPLORER.EXE)) (@Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\WSCRIPT.EXE OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\CSCRIPT.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe)) (@CommandLine:(*.lnk* OR *.bat* OR *.cmd*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/explorer\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(cmd|wscript|cscript|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/\.(lnk|bat|cmd)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name=explorer.exe Processes.process_name IN (cmd.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe, powershell.exe) (Processes.process="*.bat*" OR Processes.process="*.cmd*" OR Processes.process="*python*" OR Processes.process="*.cat*" OR Processes.process="*.lnk*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(curl|bitsadmin|certutil|wget|invoke-webrequest|downloadfile|python\.org)") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name=explorer.exe Processes.process_name IN (cmd.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe, powershell.exe) (Processes.process="*.bat*" OR Processes.process="*.cmd*" OR Processes.process="*python*" OR Processes.process="*.cat*" OR Processes.process="*.lnk*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(process, "(?i)(curl|bitsadmin|certutil|wget|invoke-webrequest|downloadfile|python\.org)") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
APT37 NarwhalRAT staging directory — %APPDATA%\naverwhale masquerading as Naver Whale browser AIInstallation High
Hunts creation of the hidden %APPDATA%\naverwhale directory used by NarwhalRAT to stage keystrokes, screenshots, audio recordings, USB exfil, and active-window captures. The directory name impersonates South Korean Naver Whale browser to evade analyst review of APPDATA contents. Rationale: %APPDATA%\naverwhale is a direct article-specific IOC (Genians reports it is NarwhalRAT's hard-coded staging directory). Excluding the legitimate Naver Whale browser binaries removes the only realistic FP source. Path is uncommon in Western enterprise estates — very low base rate. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/blog/threat_intelligence
ATT&CKT1564 T1036.005 T1074.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Korean-localised endpoint with Naver Whale browser writing genuine user profile data to APPDATA
  • Backup utility (Veeam Agent, Acronis) snapshotting an existing Naver Whale profile to a quarantine path
  • Endpoint-migration tools copying profile data between user shells
  • Anti-virus scanning the naverwhale folder and re-emitting file_write events on the same path
Response runbook
Triage: Verify whether genuine Naver Whale is installed via Get-AppxPackage / registry uninstall keys — if absent, the directory is malicious. Capture the directory contents (logs, screenshots, USB exfil staged here) for forensics. Contain: Isolate the device, kill the python.exe process tree, and quarantine the directory. Hunt: Pivot on InitiatingProcessAccountName to identify other devices owned by the same user that may share the staging pattern, and check DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound contact to daehoat.com / novel21.co.kr / api.pcloud.com from the host.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has @"\AppData\Roaming\naverwhale" or FolderPath has @"\AppData\Roaming\Naverwhale"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("naver-whale.exe", "whale.exe", "whale-installer.exe", "naverwhalesetup.exe")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), FileCount=count(), SampleFiles=make_set(FileName, 10), Processes=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 5)
    by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\AppData\Roaming\naverwhale"
| where ActingProcessName !endswith @"\naver-whale.exe"
    and ActingProcessName !endswith @"\whale.exe"
    and ActingProcessName !endswith @"\whale-installer.exe"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), FileCount=count(), SampleFiles=make_set(TargetFileName, 10), Processes=make_set(ActingProcessName, 5)
    by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: APT37 NarwhalRAT Naverwhale Staging Directory
id: 8a3f5b21-c7d4-4e6f-9a12-3b4c5d6e7f81
status: experimental
description: Detects file writes to %APPDATA%\naverwhale, NarwhalRAT's staging directory masquerading as the South Korean Naver Whale browser.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fake-microsoft-alerts-used-to-deploy.html
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
    - attack.defense_evasion
    - attack.t1564
    - attack.t1036.005
    - attack.t1074.001
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetFilename|contains: '\AppData\Roaming\naverwhale\'
    filter_naver:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\naver-whale.exe'
            - '\whale.exe'
            - '\whale-installer.exe'
            - '\naverwhalesetup.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_naver
falsepositives:
    - Genuine Naver Whale browser installations where the legit binary is renamed
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\AppData\\Roaming\\naverwhale\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Naverwhale\\*)) -@Image:(*\\naver-whale.exe OR *\\whale.exe OR *\\whale-installer.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten regex("\\\\AppData\\\\Roaming\\\\naverwhale\\\\", field=TargetFileName, flags=i)
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/(naver-whale|whale|whale-installer|naverwhalesetup)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*\\AppData\\Roaming\\naverwhale\\*" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*\\AppData\\Roaming\\naverwhale\\*" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
APT37 NarwhalRAT persistence — scheduled task 'Microsoft*Task[Machine]' naming convention AIInstallation High
Hunts schtasks.exe creating tasks that match NarwhalRAT's distinctive naming convention (MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine, MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine, or the broader Microsoft<word>(Task|Tack)Machine pattern) used to launch the CAT-file in-memory loader. Rationale: Both task names (MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine, MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine) are verbatim from Genians' write-up. The supplementary regex matches the article-noted convention (Microsoft<word>(Task|Tack)Machine) used across both ScarCruft Python-loader campaigns. Excluding machine accounts removes the only realistic FP source on Windows. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/blog/threat_intelligence • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0067/
ATT&CKT1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal sysadmin custom tasks that follow a Microsoft-style camel-case naming convention for housekeeping
  • Third-party software installer (MSP RMM tools) creating tasks with Microsoft-prefixed cosmetic names
  • Penetration-testing engagements where the red team mimics ScarCruft naming convention
  • Endpoint-management tools (Intune Win32 wrapper) deploying tasks named after MS components
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("intunemanagementextension.exe", "sccm.exe", "ccmexec.exe") and AccountName endswith "$")
Response runbook
Triage: Run `schtasks /query /tn <taskname> /xml` on the host and inspect the Actions/Triggers — NarwhalRAT tasks call a .cat file via cmd or rundll32. Capture the called CAT file and submit for analysis. Contain: Disable and delete the scheduled task (`schtasks /Delete /TN <name> /F`), isolate the host, and revoke the user's session tokens. Hunt: Sweep the estate for the same task name in DeviceProcessEvents over 90 days, pivot on the calling CAT file path, and check DeviceNetworkEvents from the host for daehoat.com / novel21.co.kr / api.pcloud.com.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/create"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine", "MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine")
    or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"Microsoft[A-Za-z]+(Task|Tack)Machine"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has "/create"
| where CommandLine has_any ("MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine", "MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine")
    or CommandLine matches regex @"Microsoft[A-Za-z]+(Task|Tack)Machine"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: APT37 NarwhalRAT Scheduled Task Persistence
id: 7c4f3a8c-1c2b-4f5e-8d9a-b2c3d4e5f6a7
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of scheduled tasks using NarwhalRAT's distinctive Microsoft<word>(Task|Tack)Machine naming convention used to launch the CAT-file in-memory loader.
references:

author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:

logsource:

detection:

            - 'MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine'

falsepositives:
    - Internal automation that mimics Microsoft naming conventions (rare)
level: high
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 @Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE) @CommandLine:*/create* (@CommandLine:*MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine* OR @CommandLine:*MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/\/create/i
| CommandLine=/Microsoft[A-Za-z]+(Task|Tack)Machine/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe Processes.process="*/create*" (Processes.process="*MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine*" OR Processes.process="*MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rex field=process "(?i)(?<task_name>Microsoft[A-Za-z]+(Task|Tack)Machine)" | where isnotnull(task_name) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe Processes.process="*/create*" (Processes.process="*MicrosoftUserInterfacePicturesUpdateTackMachine*" OR Processes.process="*MicrosoftMusicLibrariesPackageTaskMachine*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rex field=process "(?i)(?<task_name>Microsoft[A-Za-z]+(Task|Tack)Machine)" | where isnotnull(task_name) | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
APT37 NarwhalRAT primary C2 — daehoat.com / novel21.co.kr Korean relay domains + IOC IPs AICommand & Control High
Hunts outbound DNS/network connections to NarwhalRAT's primary C2 infrastructure — Korean websites daehoat.com, novel21.co.kr (plus secondary relays fe01.co.kr, webhostingkorea.com, crwellfood.com) and the six C2 IPs Genians identified, prioritising connections initiated by python.exe or processes running out of the naverwhale staging path. Rationale: All six IPs and five domains are pulled verbatim from Genians' published IOC set. Pivoting the high-fidelity tier on python.exe or %APPDATA%\naverwhale-resident processes ties the C2 contact to the article's exact malware family, eliminating noise from any legitimate Korean web traffic on these shared-hosting IPs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/blog/threat_intelligence
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Korean-region employees legitimately browsing daehoat.com or novel21.co.kr news content
  • Threat-intel analyst / sandbox host resolving the IOCs deliberately for investigation
  • Shared web-hosting IPs (these are Korean ISPs) hosting unrelated benign tenants
  • Internal proxy logs surfacing test/canary requests to flagged domains
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msedge.exe", "chrome.exe", "firefox.exe") and AccountName !endswith "$")
Response runbook
Triage: Confirm the InitiatingProcessFileName — python.exe or anything from %APPDATA%\naverwhale is HIGH severity; browser processes are likely REVIEW. Pull packet captures or proxy logs for the session. Contain: Block the five domains at DNS firewall and the six IPs at the perimeter, isolate the host, kill python.exe. Hunt: Search DeviceFileEvents on the host for the naverwhale directory, schtasks for the UC4 task names, and EmailEvents for the initial lure 30 days back.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("121.254.222.10", "121.254.222.80", "211.239.157.126", "218.150.78.198", "218.150.78.231", "61.100.9.206")
    or RemoteUrl has_any ("daehoat.com", "novel21.co.kr", "fe01.co.kr", "webhostingkorea.com", "crwellfood.com")
| extend HighFidelity = iff(
    InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe", "pythonw.exe") 
      or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "naverwhale"
      or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "cmd.exe"
      or InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "schtasks.exe",
    "HIGH", "REVIEW")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, HighFidelity
| order by Timestamp desc
let IocIPs = dynamic(["121.254.222.10", "121.254.222.80", "211.239.157.126", "218.150.78.198", "218.150.78.231", "61.100.9.206"]);
let IocDomains = dynamic(["daehoat.com", "novel21.co.kr", "fe01.co.kr", "webhostingkorea.com", "crwellfood.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where Name has_any (IocDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Source="DNS", Indicator=Name, Process=""),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DestinationIP in (IocIPs) or RequestURL has_any (IocDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (IocDomains)
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DeviceName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Source="Firewall", Indicator=coalesce(RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP), Process=DeviceProcessId)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: APT37 NarwhalRAT C2 Network Contact
id: 4d2f1b8a-3e6c-4a7b-9f1d-2c3b4a5d6e7f
status: experimental
description: Detects network connections to NarwhalRAT C2 infrastructure (daehoat.com / novel21.co.kr / fe01.co.kr and 6 Korean ISP IPs).
references:

author: Detection Engineering

logsource:

detection:

APT37 NarwhalRAT secondary C2 — pCloud API with folderid/auth dead-drop parameters AICommand & Control High
Hunts non-pCloud-client processes contacting api.pcloud.com / eapi.pcloud.com with the folderid and auth query parameters NarwhalRAT uses as a dead-drop resolver. The article calls out these exact parameter names as the differentiator between legitimate pCloud client traffic and the malware's covert channel. Rationale: Genians explicitly names 'folderid' and 'auth' as the pCloud API parameters NarwhalRAT processes — these are the differentiator from genuine pCloud client traffic. Restricting initiator to python.exe / pythonw.exe / naverwhale-resident binaries (the article's stack) makes this near-zero FP. URL parameter visibility requires a web proxy or Sysmon EID 22 / Defender Web Content Filtering — Sentinel branch uses ImWebSession for that telemetry path. Cross-checked against: • https://www.genians.co.kr/blog/threat_intelligence
ATT&CKT1102.001 T1567.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer testing pCloud REST API from a Python script for legitimate cloud storage automation
  • Backup automation tooling using pCloud Python SDK with the same folderid/auth parameters
  • Penetration test scripts emulating pCloud dead-drop techniques for control validation
  • DevOps CI runners that legitimately push artifacts to pCloud via Python SDK
Suppression filter
and not (AccountName has_any ("svc-backup", "devops-") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pcloud-sdk", "pcloudapi"))
Response runbook
Triage: Capture the full URL query string (folderid value reveals the dead-drop folder, auth token can be revoked via pCloud abuse contact). Pull the python.exe command line and any script file referenced. Contain: Block *.pcloud.com at the proxy for the affected host, isolate the device, kill python.exe, and rotate any local credentials that may have been exfiltrated. Hunt: Pivot on the folderid value across the org's proxy logs to find other infected hosts using the same dead-drop, and check DeviceFileEvents for naverwhale staging + UC4 scheduled task names.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "pcloud.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("pcloudsync.exe", "pcloud.exe", "pcloudbackup.exe", "msedge.exe", "chrome.exe", "firefox.exe", "brave.exe", "iexplore.exe", "opera.exe", "msedgewebview2.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe", "pythonw.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "naverwhale"
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("folderid", "auth=", "api.pcloud", "eapi.pcloud")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has "pcloud.com"
| where Url has_any ("folderid", "auth=")
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("Mozilla", "Chrome", "Edge", "Firefox", "Safari", "pcloud")
    or isempty(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstHostname, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpMethod
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| NOT ContextImageFileName=/(pcloud|pcloudsync|msedge|chrome|firefox|brave|iexplore|opera)\.exe$/i
| (ContextImageFileName=/(python|pythonw)\.exe$/i OR regex("naverwhale", field=ContextImageFileName, flags=i))

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count

    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b") or SHA1 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b") or MD5 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b") or SHA1 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b") or MD5 in~ ("3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["3715092aa00f380cefe8b4d2eddb7d08", "7cef19f9c4480adac0cd4702ff98f46c", "7eb9cee1f696727752169f25cf79a338", "b6b0602310bb2d4360c52685119aac1b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental

            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files

ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"

                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-61882", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073")

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-61882", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073")

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("8974830446d35e234881696092aded87", "ef970697c5094c443f0456774cfee9bc", "935413b08ef60cd819b2e1b573fc9050", "2163afa18a3cdfa525b767e0e1baaba1", "1827aa636cd86d1a4064e112aa197303", "00b69eb7f44b5987f68667343aaafb6a", "01ab231bcd9533f90e99651521b6e1bb") or SHA1 in~ ("8974830446d35e234881696092aded87", "ef970697c5094c443f0456774cfee9bc", "935413b08ef60cd819b2e1b573fc9050", "2163afa18a3cdfa525b767e0e1baaba1", "1827aa636cd86d1a4064e112aa197303", "00b69eb7f44b5987f68667343aaafb6a", "01ab231bcd9533f90e99651521b6e1bb") or MD5 in~ ("8974830446d35e234881696092aded87", "ef970697c5094c443f0456774cfee9bc", "935413b08ef60cd819b2e1b573fc9050", "2163afa18a3cdfa525b767e0e1baaba1", "1827aa636cd86d1a4064e112aa197303", "00b69eb7f44b5987f68667343aaafb6a", "01ab231bcd9533f90e99651521b6e1bb")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("8974830446d35e234881696092aded87", "ef970697c5094c443f0456774cfee9bc", "935413b08ef60cd819b2e1b573fc9050", "2163afa18a3cdfa525b767e0e1baaba1", "1827aa636cd86d1a4064e112aa197303", "00b69eb7f44b5987f68667343aaafb6a", "01ab231bcd9533f90e99651521b6e1bb") or SHA1 in~ ("8974830446d35e234881696092aded87", "ef970697c5094c443f0456774cfee9bc", "935413b08ef60cd819b2e1b573fc9050", "2163afa18a3cdfa525b767e0e1baaba1", "1827aa636cd86d1a4064e112aa197303", "00b69eb7f44b5987f68667343aaafb6a", "01ab231bcd9533f90e99651521b6e1bb") or MD5 in~ ("8974830446d35e234881696092aded87", "ef970697c5094c443f0456774cfee9bc", "935413b08ef60cd819b2e1b573fc9050", "2163afa18a3cdfa525b767e0e1baaba1", "1827aa636cd86d1a4064e112aa197303", "00b69eb7f44b5987f68667343aaafb6a", "01ab231bcd9533f90e99651521b6e1bb")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["8974830446d35e234881696092aded87", "ef970697c5094c443f0456774cfee9bc", "935413b08ef60cd819b2e1b573fc9050", "2163afa18a3cdfa525b767e0e1baaba1", "1827aa636cd86d1a4064e112aa197303", "00b69eb7f44b5987f68667343aaafb6a", "01ab231bcd9533f90e99651521b6e1bb"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

CVE-2026-54420 LiteSpeed cPanel exploit: generateEcCert chained to packageUserSize for same user AIExploitation High
Detects the specific exploitation pattern for CVE-2026-54420 where an attacker with FTP/web shell access on a CloudLinux/CageFS shared host invokes the cPanel JSON API function `generateEcCert` immediately followed by `packageUserSize` for the same cPanel user within seconds. LiteSpeed explicitly states legitimate UI flows never chain these two calls — this is the highest-fidelity signature published by the vendor. Rationale: Anchored on the EXACT IOC strings published by LiteSpeed in the article body (`cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert`, `cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize`, `cert_action_entry.*geneccert`) and the vendor's explicit statement that legitimate UI flows never chain these two calls for the same user. The 10-second correlation window is generous; LiteSpeed says the calls are 'immediately' chained, so most true positives will be sub-second. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-54420
ATT&CKT1068 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Hosting provider's own automation tool (e.g. WHM bulk-provisioning script) that legitimately issues both API calls for the same user during account setup
  • Custom reseller tooling that wraps cPanel API for SSL cert provisioning and disk-quota reporting in one workflow
  • Load-testing or QA suite hammering both API endpoints
  • Migration utility (e.g. transfer_tool) that batches per-user operations
  • cPanel auto-renewal cron job if it has been customised to also report user disk usage in the same flow
Suppression filter
| where User !in~ ("root", "cpanel", "nobody") and User !startswith "_" // exclude system-context calls
| where SrcIp !in ("127.0.0.1", "::1") // exclude localhost (WHM UI proxies through loopback in some configs)
Response runbook
1) Triage: Pull the offending log lines via the LiteSpeed grep command on the affected server and confirm the chain is for ONE cPanel user (legitimate concurrent admin work would span many). Check `whoami`/`id` history and recent root-owned file creations under /home/<user>. 2) Contain: Immediately upgrade the LiteSpeed WHM Plugin to v5.3.2.1+ (bundles cPanel plugin v2.4.8). If patching is blocked, suspend the implicated cPanel user account and any FTP credentials. Snapshot the box for forensics before remediation. 3) Hunt: Search for new root-owned binaries, modified /etc/passwd or /etc/sudoers, new SSH keys in /root/.ssh, and outbound C2 from the host since the first observation. Pivot on SrcIp across other tenants of the shared host.
// Defender XDR does not natively ingest cPanel access logs. This query targets MDE-for-Linux hosts where cPanel logs are forwarded into /var/log via rsyslog and surfaced through DeviceEvents AdditionalFields, OR detects an admin running the LiteSpeed verification grep on a potentially-compromised server.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("cpanel","whm","cloudlinux") or FolderPath has "/usr/local/cpanel/"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("grep","cpanel_jsonapi_func") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("generateEcCert","packageUserSize","geneccert")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 1d;
let WindowSec = 10;
let GenCalls = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
    | where SyslogMessage has "cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert"
    | extend User = coalesce(extract(@"cpanel_jsonapi_user=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"cpanel_jsonuser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"\suser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage))
    | extend SrcIp = extract(@"((?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3})", 1, SyslogMessage)
    | project GenTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, User, SrcIp, GenMsg = SyslogMessage;
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where SyslogMessage has "cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize"
| extend User = coalesce(extract(@"cpanel_jsonapi_user=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"cpanel_jsonuser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage), extract(@"\suser=([^&\s]+)", 1, SyslogMessage))
| join kind=inner GenCalls on Computer, User
| where TimeGenerated between (GenTime .. GenTime + WindowSec * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, GenTime)
| project FirstCall_generateEcCert = GenTime, SecondCall_packageUserSize = TimeGenerated, DelaySec, Computer, User, SrcIp, GenMsg, PackageMsg = SyslogMessage
| order by FirstCall_generateEcCert desc
source:linux.syslog (@process.name:cpanel* OR @host:(*cpanel* OR *whm*)) ("cpanel_jsonapi_func=generateEcCert" OR "cpanel_jsonapi_func=packageUserSize" OR "cert_action_entry" "geneccert")

| transaction dest user maxspan=10s mvlist=t
